title: Practice 3: Running, swimming, climbing, crawling, dragging

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Он ___ (бежать — to run, one way) навстречу ветру.
exercises.why: **бежит** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти. Note that in the conjugation of the verb "бежать", the consonants "ж" and "г" are alternated: я бегу, ты бежишь, они бегут. Note also that in all persons, except the 3rd person plural, it belongs to the 2nd conjugation: ты бежишь, он бежит, мы бежим, вы бежите. In the 3rd person plural it belongs to the 1st conjugation: они бегут.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  «навстречу» gives a direction or a moment: one way, in progress, so the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **катитесь** is the present tense (2nd person plural) of **катиться** (to roll) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **кататься** for many directions. present: я качу́сь · ты ка́тишься · он ка́тится · мы ка́тимся · вы ка́титесь · они ка́тятся. — Wiktionary, «катиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Мне нравится кататься на лыжах, на коньках, на велосипеде и на лодке. — I like to ski, skate, cycle, and row.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Слёзы ___ (катиться — to roll (oneself)) по её лицу.

exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.prompt: The children are riding the carousel.

exercises.q: When Ahmad was a boy, he could climb tall trees.
exercises.why: **лазить** (the infinitive) (to climb, to clamber) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лезть** for one direction. — Wiktionary, «лазить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «умел» speaks of ability or liking — general motion, again the many-directions verb.  The other choice: **лезть** is from **лезть**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
